title: Most reliable ways to reach Grok Bots outside the desktop app
summary: Ranked paths for talking to Grok Bots away from the desktop window: mobile companion first, then Slack/channel listeners, event routines, and webhook wakes — not undocumented gateways or custom Slack apps.

sections.heading: Best paths (ranked)
bullets: 1) iOS / Android companion apps — same Bots and threads as desktop; cloud work continues if the phone sleeps. Official FAQ: primary place to talk to Grok Bot alongside desktop.

2) Connected messaging channels (Slack, Teams where supported) — channel listener routines wake a Bot; for Slack invite @Cursor into the channel (/invite @Cursor). Text/attachments only (no in-app widgets).
3) Event listeners on routines — GitHub, Slack/Teams patterns, Linear/Sentry/PagerDuty when connected; high reliability when scoped correctly.
4) Webhook routines — Add trigger → Webhook → URL + bearer key; good for wake + saved prompt from n8n/Actions/etc., not a full duplex chat API. Protect the key; optional Hookdeck in front.

sources.label: Grok Bot FAQ — where to talk
Cursor forum: message Grok Bot from outside

sections.heading: Pros / cons by path
bullets: Mobile — Pros: real conversation UX, synced threads. Cons: still the Grok Bot product, not email/SMS.
Slack/channels — Pros: meets you at work; reliable when Cursor is invited. Cons: uses Cursor’s Slack app, not your custom Slack bot.
Event listeners — Pros: first-party, no polling. Cons: only for supported event shapes.
Webhooks — Pros: wake from anywhere. Cons: routine wake ≠ desktop chat session; key security matters.

sources.label: Eric Zakariasson — webhook wake announcement context

sections.heading: What is not reliable
bullets: Undocumented local/gateway hacks — break across updates.
Custom Slack app ≠ Cursor Slack — built-in listeners will not hear it.
Email/SMS as a first-class Bot inbox — not a core Grok Bot chat surface today.
Expecting webhook = full chat API — it runs a saved routine prompt.
